reden: Yes. The audit report explicitly describes the same duplicate order-hash issue for partial fills resulting in locked assets. Findings such as “Identical partial fills create the same rental hash; second rental can never be stopped” (Storage.addRentals) and “Identical partial fills in one block collide on the rental order hash and double-count rentedAssets and escrow” (Create._rentFromZone) match the vulnerability’s root cause: _deriveRentalOrderHash produces the same hash for multiple partial fills, Storage.addRentals stores a boolean without guarding duplicates, removeRentals deletes the key once, and the second stop reverts with OrderDoesNotExist, leaving assets locked. The attack path and code locations (Signer._deriveRentalOrderHash, Create._rentFromZone, Storage.addRentals/removeRentals) are the same, and proposed fixes (nonce/uniqueness or disallow partial) would address both. Differences in severity labeling do not change that it is the same vulnerability.
